claims.text: Every free-text and every path channel of a turn.
claims.why: The function scans evidence paths, content, role, actor, vendor, model, lane, reason, refs, withheld, evidence paths, meta strings, and independence_class vendor/family.

claims.text: Returns the rule label that fired (a fixed string -- NEVER matched text), or None.
claims.why: The function returns the result of _scan_texts, but _scan_texts is defined elsewhere in the file; this chunk cannot verify that it returns a fixed label rather than matched text.

claims.text: withheld: content channel ONLY (see the carve-out in the module docstring).
claims.why: The comment claims a carve-out in the module docstring, but the module docstring is not in this chunk; the code does include withheld in texts.

claims.text: Independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not of endpoints: local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets. The class is (vendor, model family) and is mandatory.
claims.why: The function requires exactly {'vendor','family'} and raises otherwise, enforcing that the class is vendor/family and mandatory.

claims.text: Fill the dcouncil/1 turn envelope, fail-closed. Absence is REPORTED, never guessed favourably.
claims.why: The function validates actor, status, content, reason, evidence, independence_class, and meta; missing values are replaced with 'unknown' or '' rather than inferred from context.

claims.text: A refused turn's stand-in. Carries the rule LABEL only -- never the matched text, never the content, never the evidence paths (the offending path is often the secret).
claims.why: The function sets content to '', refs to [], evidence to [], withheld to [], and reason to the rule label.

claims.text: ``anonymous`` drops even the identity fields, for when the identity itself tripped the floor.
claims.why: When anonymous is True, actor becomes 'council.redacted.redacted', vendor 'redacted', model 'unknown', independence_class {'vendor':'redacted','family':'redacted'}, role 'participant', lane 'untrusted', and meta is _norm_meta(None).

claims.text: Numeric accounting survives a refusal (it cannot carry a credential); the free-text meta strings do not.
claims.why: When anonymous is False, meta keeps transport and latency_ms (numeric), dropping cli_version, endpoint, started_ts, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd. When anonymous, meta is None, dropping all.

claims.text: Tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, cached and invalidated by file signature. MUST be called under ``_WRITE_LOCK``. Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale ``prev`` can never be bound.
claims.why: The function uses _file_sig to compare cached sig; if different, reloads via load_transcript and recomputes tail/count/turns. The lock requirement and cross-process invalidation are documented; the code does not enforce the lock but the claim is about behavior under correct use.

claims.text: Chain a pre-ORDERED batch and append it. One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ``ts`` is inside ``entry_sha``, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order. Read-then-write happens inside the lock so a concurrent append can neither tear a line nor bind two lines to one ``prev``. A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline so this batch lands as its own parseable lines instead of fusing onto the fragment and being destroyed while the caller holds a success id.
claims.why: The function uses a single ts for all records, calls _chain_state under _WRITE_LOCK, and writes a leading newline if _ends_without_newline returns True.

claims.text: A check that CANNOT FAIL: an assertion comparing something with itself, a test whose fixture is derived from the thing under test, a branch no input reaches.
claims.why: No such check is visible in this chunk; all branches appear reachable given appropriate inputs.

claims.text: A refusal with NO REACHABLE REPAIR: code that reports an error and names a fix another rule in this same file forbids.
claims.why: No error message names a repair that another rule in this chunk forbids; all published repairs (e.g., use evidence_ref, use machine reason) are consistent with the normalization rules.

claims.text: A rule INVERTED with respect to its own stated goal: it blocks the narrow precise action and permits the broad one.
claims.why: No inverted rule detected; the code consistently blocks broad unverified inputs (e.g., unknown fields, arbitrary evidence shapes) and permits narrow verified ones.

claims.text: A value parsed from output whose FORMAT IS NOT PINNED: a parser that will silently report 'absent' rather than 'unreadable' when its input changes shape.
claims.why: No output parsing occurs in this chunk; only file signature and transcript loading (load_transcript defined elsewhere) are used.

observations.what: _norm_meta validates allowed keys via _reject_unknown, but the returned dict uses m.get with defaults; if a caller passes an allowed key with a non-string value, it is coerced to string implicitly? Actually no, values are passed through as-is; the claim 'absence is REPORTED' holds, but non-string values are not type-checked.

_refusal_receipt when anonymous=False keeps latency_ms and transport but drops started_ts and other numeric fields like prompt_tokens; the comment says 'Numeric accounting survives' but latency_ms is the only numeric kept; prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd are dropped even though numeric. This contradicts the comment's broad claim.

_normalize_turn allows 'budget_exhausted' status with reason forced to 'budget_exhausted', but the docstring says 'Absence is REPORTED' -- this is a guess, not a report, though it's a machine-determined reason.

_chain_records writes a prefix newline only if the tail lacks one, but if the file is empty (size 0), _ends_without_newline returns False, so no leading newline is written; the first line is written correctly. This is fine.

_chain_state caches by file path and signature; if the file is deleted, _file_sig returns None and the cache is bypassed, but load_transcript may fail if file missing -- however, _chain_records creates parent dir and appends, so file should exist.

risks: _refusal_receipt | medium | The comment claims 'Numeric accounting survives a refusal' but only latency_ms is preserved; prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd are dropped even though numeric. This could mislead readers about what survives. | Check whether the intent is to preserve all numeric meta fields or only latency; if so, the code is incomplete.
